Every Room

Every songwriter's world is a room.
This is the whole building.

One map of who has written with whom across these catalogs. Here's how to read it and use it.
  1. 1
    Everyone is on one mapEach dot is a writer or an artist. A line between two people means they've been in a room together, credited on the same song. Bigger, brighter dots have more of them.
  2. 2
    Find anyone, open their worldSearch a name at the top, or tap any dot to open that person and see everyone they've been in a room with.
  3. 3
    Spot the connectorsThe white dots that pulse are connectors, the people who bridge multiple worlds. Tap "Super connectors" to light up the biggest bridges on the map.
  4. 4
    Trace the path between two peoplePick two names and trace the line between them. You'll see up to ten ways they connect, most direct first, so you can find the warmest introduction into any room.
  5. 5
    That's the whole ideaSame rooms, never the same room, yet. Find the shortest path into the room you want, then get in it.
